Subject: RFP Clarification — commercial section (commits & burst handling)

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the RFP response. Our procurement team has a couple of clarifying questions specifically about the commercial model in section C: how committed monthly token volumes, overage rates, and burst smoothing would work during seasonal spikes. A few concrete asks: 

- Can you provide an example of how credits/overages would be calculated if we commit 150M tokens/month but spike to 300M in a given month?
- Do you support carryover of unused committed tokens or a rolling-average smoothing approach?
- What discount bands apply for annual multi-year commits vs. single-year?
- Are there any hard caps or auto-throttles that would kick in if we exceed burst thresholds?

We are looking to include these clarifications in the commercial appendix before our vendor scoring next week. Can you respond with a short worked example and the preferred contract language for "burst protection" and "overage calculation"?

Appreciate it —

MedTech Systems

Subject: Re: RFP Clarification — commercial section (commits & burst handling)

Hi Alicia —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise worked example plus contractual wording we recommend including. I've looped in Connor (pricing) and Laura (commercial ops) to confirm the numbers and DocuSign flow.

Summary (short): Redwood supports committed-monthly tokens with three smoothing mechanisms we recommend: 1) carryover credits (unused committed tokens carry forward for 3 months), 2) burst buffer (a shared cushion equal to 30% of monthly commit usable up to 2x per quarter), and 3) rolling-average billing (12-week moving average to moderate one-off spikes when requested). Overage pricing and discount bands are shown in the example below.

Worked example (committed = 150M tokens/month):
- Month baseline: 150M committed
- Month observed: 300M tokens consumed (one-off spike)
- Carryover: assume prior two months had combined 40M unused tokens (carried forward) -> available credits = 40M
- Burst buffer: 30% of 150M = 45M available as burst buffer for this month (policy allows 2 uses per quarter)
- Smoothing application order: carryover credits -> burst buffer -> rolling-average adjustment -> overage billing

Calculation: 300M observed - (150M committed + 40M carryover + 45M burst buffer) = 65M tokens billed as overage for the month.

Pricing model (example unit rates):
- Committed tier effective rate (applied to committed units): $0.95 per 1K tokens (equivalent to $950 per 1M tokens) at 150M/month commit
- Overage rate (after smoothing): $1.35 per 1K tokens (higher to reflect on-demand bursts)
- Peak surge (if burst buffer exhausted and no rolling smoothing allowed): $1.75 per 1K tokens
- Multi-year commit discount: additional 8% for 2-year, 15% for 3-year (applied to effective committed rate)

Example dollars for the month above: 65M overage tokens at $1.35 per 1K = $87,750 overage charge (rounded). Committed spend remains priced at the committed effective rate for the 150M.

Contract language snippets (suggested additions to commercial appendix):
- "Carryover Credits: Unused committed tokens may be carried forward for up to three (3) consecutive months and applied to subsequent usage. Carryover credit expiration is month-end of the third month after issuance."
- "Burst Buffer: Customer is entitled to a burst buffer equal to thirty percent (30%) of the committed monthly token volume. Burst buffer usage is limited to two (2) distinct months per calendar quarter unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- "Rolling-Average Smoothing: At Customer request, Redwood may apply a rolling average of up to twelve (12) weeks to moderate charges for one-off spikes; application is subject to mutual agreement and may require manual invoice reconciliation."
- "Overage Rate Escalation: If bursts exceed the burst buffer and rolling-average smoothing is not elected, overage units will be billed at the rate specified in the pricing schedule for peak surges."

Attachments: I attached a short worked-example spreadsheet (Redwood-Commit-Flex-Worked-Example.xlsx) with a few scenarios. Connor/Laura — pls confirm whether we should change the numeric rates or the burst buffer % before I send a final RFP response.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Quick internal note / then brief external update.

Soojin / Laura — I've reviewed the worked example. Two adjustments I recommend before we finalize:
1) Reduce the committed effective rate slightly for the 150M tier to $0.88 per 1K tokens (reflecting volume pricing for MedTech) — that keeps the math tidy and gives them a visible ~7% sticker discount vs. our example.
2) Add a "burst reconstitution" clause: if burst buffer used, Redwood will replenish burst buffer at 50% of its size the following month (one-time) to help recovery months. This is customer-friendly and limits billing surprise.

Alicia — happy to confirm publicly that we can offer the revised committed rate and the replenishment clause. Laura, can we reflect the rate in the SOW and prepare an initial DocuSign for a 12-month term with optional 2- and 3-year extensions (2-year gets +8% discount; 3-year +15% as outlined)?

Connor
Pricing Lead, Redwood Inference
